Compute Gower distances and the hierarchical clustering tree

Source: R/assess_gower.R
assess_gower.Rd

Computes the Gower dissimilarity between strains (suited to categorical metadata) and performs an agglomerative hierarchical clustering with complete linkage.

Usage

assess_gower(clean_data, weights = rep.int(1, p), graph = TRUE)

Source

Adapted from the dissimilarity matrix and agglomerative clustering steps of Anastasia Reusova's tutorial: Reusova A. (2018). Hierarchical Clustering on Categorical Data in R. Towards Data Science. https://medium.com/@anastasia.reusova/hierarchical-clustering-on-categorical-data-in-r-a27e578f2995. Code: https://github.com/khunreus/cluster-categorical.

Arguments

clean_data

A data frame of factors, one row per strain, as returned by prepare_input().

weights

Numeric vector of weights, one per column of clean_data, to give more or less importance to each metadata. Defaults to equal weights.

graph

If TRUE (default), the dendrogram is plotted.

Value

A list with two components:

gower_dist

the Gower dissimilarity matrix, an object of class dissimilarity / dist (see cluster::daisy());

aggl.clust.c

the clustering tree, an object of class hclust.

See also

Other clustering method: cstats_table(), export_selection(), report_selection(), select_silhouette(), select_strains()

Examples

raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
#> no duplicate ID
#> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = TRUE)
